steps.prompt: Use the signed-in GitHub CLI through Bash(gh *) on macOS because GitHub has a first-class CLI. arguments.name: github-stale-pr-review-nudges
arguments.title: Remind reviewers of aging pull requests
arguments.summary: Find open pull requests awaiting review for more than two days and post one friendly reminder tagging each requested reviewer.
arguments.description: Assuming a weekday morning cadence, run every weekday at 9am to find open acme/api pull requests that have awaited review for more than two days and comment with a gentle reviewer reminder on each qualifying PR.
arguments.generalization: The recording checked and commented on one PR; each run will enumerate all matching open PRs, verify their exact age and outstanding review requests, and avoid posting the same reminder again. The repo and age threshold are fixed editable values; PR numbers, dates, and reviewers are discovered at run time.

values.name: Reminder wording
values.value: Friendly ping — this PR has been waiting on review for a couple of days, could you take a look?

steps.label: Find aging PRs
steps.prompt: On this Windows device, use PowerShell and the signed-in `gh` CLI (Bash(gh *)). Compute the ISO created-date cutoff at run time from {{age_days}} days ago; query open PRs in {{repo}} with `gh pr list -R {{repo}} --state open --search 'review:required created:<DATE sort:created-asc' --json number,title,createdAt,reviewRequests,author --limit 10000`, replacing DATE with the computed date. Use `gh` because GitHub has a first-class CLI; stop with a clear prerequisite failure if it is unavailable or unauthenticated. Handle every returned PR, not just the oldest example.

steps.label: Verify review wait
steps.prompt: For each candidate in {{repo}}, use `gh pr view NUMBER -R {{repo}} --json number,createdAt,reviewRequests,comments` to confirm it is still open, its exact createdAt timestamp is more than {{age_days}} days old, and it has outstanding requested reviewers. Check existing comments to skip PRs already given this reminder by the current signed-in account, so scheduled runs do not repost it. Resolve the requested reviewer login(s) from reviewRequests at run time; skip candidates without an outstanding requested reviewer.

steps.label: Post reviewer reminders
steps.prompt: For every remaining PR in {{repo}}, tag its outstanding requested reviewer login(s) and post the friendly text {{reminder_text}} as a new PR comment using `gh pr comment NUMBER -R {{repo}} --body TEXT` (Bash(gh *)). Compose TEXT with the actual @login mention(s) followed by the reminder text; comment once per qualifying PR. Report the PR numbers commented on and any skipped or failed cases.

results.finalMessage: I proposed a weekday 9 a.m. automation that checks all open PRs in `acme/api`, verifies which have awaited review for more than two days, and posts one gentle comment tagging each requested reviewer. The schedule and fixed values are ready for your review.

arguments.description: Every weekday at 9am, review new inbound leads in the Sales Leads mailbox, verify each person through LinkedIn, and create qualified Salesforce contacts.

steps.prompt: Use workiq_search_emails, workiq_list_emails, and workiq_get_email to find messages in {{lead_mailbox}} received since the last successful run. arguments.title: Triage unassigned bug reports
arguments.description: Daily at 9:00 a.m. local time, check acme/api for open, unassigned bug issues; ask reporters for exact reproduction steps and their version, then label each issue needs-info. The daily schedule is a proposed default for review.
arguments.summary: Request missing reproduction details on every eligible bug issue and mark it needs-info.
arguments.generalization: The recording handled one issue. Each run finds all currently open, unassigned bug issues that have not been marked needs-info, checks each issue's current state and comments, and handles every eligible issue. The label prevents repeat comments on later runs; checking comments also recovers safely if a prior run commented but did not finish labeling.

values.name: Reporter request
values.value: Thanks for the report! Could you share exact reproduction steps and the version you're on?

steps.label: Find eligible issues
steps.prompt: Use the device shell with Bash(gh *) and the signed-in GitHub CLI because GitHub has a native CLI. Run `gh issue list -R {{repo}} --state open --label {{bug_label}} --search 'no:assignee -label:{{needs_info_label}}' --json number,title --limit 100000` and collect every matching issue; paginate further if needed so no issue is skipped. If gh is unavailable or not authenticated, stop with a clear prerequisite failure.

steps.label: Check each report
steps.prompt: For every issue found, use Bash(gh *) to run `gh issue view NUMBER -R {{repo}} --json state,assignees,labels,body,comments`. Confirm it is still open, unassigned, labeled {{bug_label}}, and lacks {{needs_info_label}}. Check whether the exact {{request_comment}} was already posted by this account; if so, do not post it again, but continue to the labeling step.

steps.label: Ask for details
steps.prompt: For each still-eligible issue without this account's prior request, use Bash(gh *) to run `gh issue comment NUMBER -R {{repo}} --body "{{request_comment}}"`. Comment on every eligible issue and record which comments succeeded. Do not label an issue if its comment fails.

steps.label: Mark waiting for info
steps.prompt: For each still-eligible issue whose request comment was just posted or was already present from this account, use Bash(gh *) to run `gh issue edit NUMBER -R {{repo}} --add-label {{needs_info_label}}`. arguments.title: Nudge stale PR reviews
arguments.summary: Find open PRs awaiting review for over two days and comment with a friendly reviewer reminder.
arguments.description: Assuming a weekday morning review cadence, run every weekday at 9am local device time; find open pull requests in acme/api that have awaited review for more than two days and post a gentle reminder tagging their requested reviewers, avoiding duplicate recent nudges.
arguments.generalization: The recording checked and commented on one PR. Each run queries the full open PR collection, verifies the exact age and pending review request for every candidate, then comments once on each eligible PR.

steps.label: Find review candidates
steps.prompt: On this Windows device, use PowerShell and the signed-in GitHub CLI (`Bash(gh *)`). Compute an ISO date cutoff at run time for {{age_days}} days ago, then run `gh pr list -R {{repo}} --state open --search 'review:required created:<YYYY-MM-DD' --json number,title,createdAt,reviewRequests,url` with the computed date substituted into the search string. Use `gh` because it is GitHub's first-class CLI. If `gh` is unavailable or unauthenticated, stop with a clear prerequisite failure.

steps.label: Check every PR
steps.prompt: For every returned PR, use `gh pr view -R {{repo}} <number> --json createdAt,reviewRequests,reviews,comments,url` and, if needed, `gh api repos/{{repo}}/pulls/<number>/requested_reviewers` to confirm it is still open, older than {{age_days}} full 24-hour days, and has pending requested reviewers. Use `gh api repos/{{repo}}/issues/<number>/comments` to inspect recent comments; skip a PR if this automation already posted a reviewer reminder within the past {{age_days}} days. Collect the requested reviewers' GitHub handles for each eligible PR.

steps.label: Post gentle reminders

Use `gh pr comment -R {{repo}} <number> --body <message>` via `Bash(gh *)`. Keep the message concise and specific to the review request; never comment on PRs with no pending requested reviewer. Report the PRs commented on and any skipped or failed PRs.

steps.label: Find and update the checkout
steps.prompt: Use glob to locate a local checkout whose git remote is {{repo}} and which contains package.json and {{changelog}}; stop with a prerequisite failure if none exists. arguments.name: weekday-inbound-leads-to-salesforce
arguments.title: Qualify inbound leads and create Salesforce contacts
arguments.summary: Review new Sales Leads emails, verify each person on LinkedIn, and create matching Salesforce contacts.
arguments.description: Assuming a weekday morning cadence, run every weekday at 9am to process all new inbound sales leads from the Sales Leads mailbox, verify them on LinkedIn, and create Salesforce contacts for qualified leads.
arguments.generalization: The two people in the recording are examples. On each run, collect every new unprocessed lead in the mailbox, iterate over all lead records found in the messages, verify each person's identity and company, and create a contact only if Salesforce has no matching contact.

steps.label: Collect new leads
steps.prompt: Use workiq_search_emails and workiq_list_emails to find every new, unprocessed inbound sales-lead email in {{lead_mailbox}} since the last successful run; use workiq_get_email to read each message. Extract every lead in each message, including name, company, role, and email when present. Keep the message identifiers so later runs do not process the same leads again.

steps.label: Verify and enrich
steps.prompt: For each extracted lead, use browser_navigate to open {{linkedin_url}} in the existing authorized browser session, then browser_snapshot and the necessary browser interaction tools to search for the person and company, because this lookup used LinkedIn's web UI and no Scout LinkedIn CLI is available. Record a profile URL and corroborated role/company only when the match is clear; leave uncertain details blank and skip leads whose identity cannot be established.

steps.label: Create CRM contacts
steps.prompt: For every verified lead, use browser_navigate and browser_snapshot in Salesforce to search existing contacts by email, then by name and company where email is absent. If no matching contact exists, navigate to {{salesforce_contacts_url}}, snapshot the form, fill the available name, company/account, email, role/title, and verified LinkedIn URL with browser_fill_form or browser_type, and create the Salesforce contact with browser_click. Record which source leads were created or already existed so future runs can avoid duplicates. Do not create an opportunity unless the source lead explicitly requests one.

results.finalMessage: I’ve proposed the automation for your review. It assumes **weekdays at 9am** and processes every new lead in the Sales Leads mailbox, verifies each person on LinkedIn, and creates a Salesforce contact when no match exists. You can change the schedule or steps before approving it.
